Tympanic_Membrane_Ring.description: A large, distinct circular eardrum visible directly on the surface of the skin just behind the eye. Extremely efficient at picking up low-frequency croaks and mating calls over long terrestrial distances.

Subterranean_Columella.description: Lacking an external eardrum entirely, the stapes bone connects directly to the jaw and squamosal bone. It detects ultra-low frequency seismic vibrations traveling through the earth, alerting the entity to heavy footsteps miles away.

Acoustic_Resonance_Cavity.description: A hollow, air-filled chamber situated behind a thin layer of skin. This cavity perfectly resonates with extremely high-pitched whistles and insect buzzing, acting as a biological passive sonar array.

Aquatic_Lateral_Line_Extension.description: The auditory system is seamlessly integrated into a highly developed lateral line organ crossing the head. It perfectly detects minute pressure waves and water displacements, allowing hunting in absolute aquatic darkness.

Vestigial_Otic_Capsule.description: The inner ear is heavily calcified and completely decoupled from the environment. The entity is entirely deaf to airborne sounds, completely immune to sonic or thunder-based magical attacks.

Vocal_Sac_Coupled_Tympanum.description: An incredibly specialized ear structure that physically severs its connection to the eardrum when the entity's lungs inflate. This prevents the entity's own deafening, 100+ decibel mating roar from continually shattering its inner ear.

Seismic_Papilla_Amphibiorum.description: A sensory organ within the inner ear found exclusively in amphibians. It is staggeringly sensitive to low-frequency thumps, allowing a resting frog to feel a predator shifting its weight three trees over.

External_Fleshy_Ear_Baffles.description: Rare, fleshy ridges protruding slightly around the tympanic membrane. While not true pinnae like a mammal, they manage to funnel and capture sound directionally during torrential tropical downpours.

High_Frequency_Otic_Pores.description: Microscopic sensory pores ringing the skull that are hyper-tuned to the ultrasonic frequencies of bat echolocation. When pinged by high-frequency sound, it triggers an involuntary, instantaneous evasive leap.

Aposematic_Auditory_Glands.description: The tympanic membrane is backed by a highly pressurized venom sac. If the eardrum is ruptured by immense sonic force or a predator's bite, it aggressively sprays blinding toxins outward in a localized mist.
